title: The Menorah as base-network memory
statement: The corpus reads the seven-branched Menorah as preserving the operational memory of the creators' terrestrial base network: in the canon's account, the original referent was a console at the creators' headquarters bearing seven indicator lights that kept contact with the other bases and with the interplanetary craft in orbit — a status board whose meaning was lost, surviving as the lampstand specified in Exodus 25 and carried through Temple Judaism to the present; the corpus registers the Zechariah 4 vision (the seven lamps as 'the eyes of Yahweh ranging over the whole earth') as the biblical layer closest to the operational reading.

includes: The console reading as the canon states it: seven telltale lights, contact with the bases and the orbiting craft, the meaning lost — telemetry, not liturgy, at the origin
The survival claim: the design's persistence from the Exodus 25 specification through Temple furnishing to the modern emblem, carried at documentary grade as the symbol's attested history
The Zechariah registration: the seven lamps glossed as the ranging eyes of Yahweh, read as the biblical text's own closest approach to a monitoring-network description
excludes: Any claim about the number or location of the bases beyond the canon's seven; no site is identified and no geography is asserted
The mainstream iconography displaced: the botanical almond-blossom vocabulary of Exodus 25 itself and the ancient Near Eastern tree-of-life reading are carried against this record in full
Judaism's own liturgical theology of the Menorah, which is the tradition's and stays the tradition's
The corpus's emblem, which is woh-claim-0043's territory; the two symbol records do not merge

source_references.locator: TBWTT-WOH 3:294 (section 'Les hommes ne pouvaient pas comprendre', 3:262 ff.): the seven-branched lampstand as the headquarters console with seven indicator lights linking the bases and the orbiting craft
Exodus 25:31-40 (the lampstand specification and its almond-blossom vocabulary)
Zechariah 4:2, 4:10 (the seven lamps; 'the eyes of Yahweh ranging over the whole earth')

alternatives.statement: Exodus 25 itself describes the lampstand botanically — branches, calyxes, almond blossoms — and the ancient Near Eastern stylized-tree iconography accounts for the form without remainder; the text's own vocabulary is horticultural, not instrumental.
Seven is the ancient world's most overloaded number; a seven-light console read from a seven-branched lamp exemplifies the pattern-matching the corpus's own instrument records forbid.

revision_triggers: Public prose identifies base sites or extends the network claim beyond the canon's statement, which this record excludes.
Claim woh-claim-0043's scope changes in a way that touches the symbol division of labor.
The corpus's Menorah entry changes the reading's stated scope.
